title: Paul Kelly Returns to Sydney’s Kings Cross for One-Off Show
summary: Kelly will release a deluxe edition of his 2025 album Seventy two ahead of the gig.
contentText:
Paul Kelly is returning to Kings Cross for the first time in decades, announcing a one-night-only show at the Potts Point Hotel on Aug. 30 — steps from the long-gone venue where the Australian songwriter cut his teeth in the mid-1980s.

The Sydney neighbourhood looms large in Kelly’s catalogue and mythology, and his return carries a personal weight. The Potts Point Hotel sits beside the laneway that once housed the Manzil Room, a late-night haunt Kelly played repeatedly in the mid-to-late ’80s.

“A wee hours sticky-carpet venue, attracting all the denizens of the night — street workers, bohemians, drug dealers, desperadoes, off work musicians,” he recalled in a statement.

“We’d play three sets, starting around 1am. The painter Brett Whiteley sometimes dropped in to hear us.” Kelly noted the Manzil Room is now a block of apartments, musing, “I wonder if the residents sometimes hear our chattering ghosts, the faint distant throb of our music.”

Fittingly, a recently completed mural of Kelly by artist Scottie Marsh adorns the exterior wall of the Potts Point Hotel.

The show doubles as a launch. Kelly will release a deluxe edition of his 2025 album Seventy two days before the gig, and access to the intimate show is tied to the release — fans can secure a spot by pre-ordering the deluxe edition from Kelly’s official store or entering a ballot for tickets.

Separately, Kelly is marking the 40th anniversary of his landmark 1986 double album Gossip with a 2LP anniversary reissue.

Seventy , released last November to mark both Kelly’s 70th birthday and his 50th year in music, debuted at No. 2 on the ARIA Albums Chart and followed a sold-out Australian arena tour. It was his 30th studio album, extending one of the most decorated careers in Australian music.

A 17-time ARIA Award winner and ARIA Hall of Fame inductee, Kelly has topped the ARIA Albums Chart with Life Is Fine (2017) and Nature (2018), and is behind some of the most enduring songs in the national canon, including “To Her Door,” “How to Make Gravy” and “From Little Things Big Things Grow.” He was appointed an Officer of the Order of Australia in 2017 for his contribution to the performing arts.
